thread:
jane.user: Hi — my voucher 'SUMMER-DEV-2026' is being rejected as invalid when I try to redeem it in the app. I haven't used it before.

support_liz: Sorry about that, Jane. Can you paste the exact code and the email on the account?

jane.user: Code: SUMMER-DEV-2026
Email: jose.cafe@example.com (that's how I signed up)

support_liz: Thanks. Checking the promo service now. One sec. :mag_right:

support_liz: Huh — API returns 400 with payload: 
```json
{ "error": "promo_invalid", "reason": "code_not_applicable" }
```

support_liz: The promo exists in our dashboard and shows remaining uses. Not expired. Escalating to billing.

billing_mark: Looking at the promo row: 
```
code: SUMMER-DEV-2026
status: active
redeem_by_email: "josé.café@example.com"
uses_allowed: 10
uses_claimed: 0
```

billing_mark: The promo is restricted to a specific email. It looks like the DB row contains accented characters for the allowed email (josé.café@...).

jane.user: Oh! I typed jose.cafe (no accents) when I signed up — the accented version is from the customer outreach list. Could that be why it's rejecting?

support_liz: Likely. Our redemption code checks exact string equality against redeem_by_email (no normalisation). If the allowed email contains combining/accent chars, jose.cafe won't match josé.café. That makes the service treat the code as not applicable to this account, which surfaces as "promo_invalid".

eng_ash: Confirming — the promo validation path does strict equals on the stored allowed_email. We do not do Unicode normalization or ASCII-folding. db shows allowed_email stored with precomposed accented chars (NFC). The user account email is stored without accents.

eng_ash: Quick repro from staging: 
Request:
POST /v1/promos/redeem
Body: { "code": "SUMMER-DEV-2026", "email": "jose.cafe@example.com" }
Response:
HTTP/1.1 400
{ "error": "promo_invalid", "reason": "email_mismatch" }

eng_ash: If you use the accented address in the request it succeeds. So root cause is email normalization mismatch.

support_liz: For this customer, we should manually apply the credit now and follow up with engineering fixes.

billing_mark: Manual credit applied: 1000 credits, txn id txn_2026_9876. Noted in support ticket #6241. :white_check_mark:

jane.user: Thank you!! Really appreciate the quick help.

eng_ash: Action items: (1) Short-term: update promo-validate to do Unicode normalization (NFC) on both sides before comparison, plus an option to ASCII-fold for partner-provided lists. (2) Add logging when redeem_by_email mismatches to capture both stored and incoming canonical forms. (3) Run a migration to normalize existing redeem_by_email values to a consistent form.

eng_ash: I filed ENG-1423 for the change and added a unit test covering composed vs decomposed accent variants.

support_liz: I'll close the ticket after confirming Jane received the credits. Follow-up note to operations: partner outreach CSV import sometimes contains precomposed accents; include normalization in import pipeline.

redwood-bot: Ticket #6241 updated: manual credit applied by billing_mark.

jane.user: Confirmed I see the credits. Closing from my side. Thanks again everyone! :tada:
